perspective:
As Harold Padilla, the information available to me is:

- I am a project manager. Arthur Begum is my friend and a police officer; I often seek his advice.
- I felt frustrated and anxious because my project team seemed unmotivated, affecting progress. I arranged to meet Arthur at a coffee shop.
- I told Arthur my team seemed completely unmotivated and I was at my wit’s end. Arthur advised me to understand what drives each team member individually and to try one-on-one conversations. I said I would try it and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward I felt hopeful and relieved. I told my team we would have quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each person and wanted us to make the project a success together.
- Later I noticed the team still was not responding well. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- I told Arthur that his suggestions had not worked and that I was worried. Arthur suggested there might be deeper issues—personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors—and that I might need to dig deeper. I said I would set up another round of meetings.
- I became determined and focused, believing there might be unaddressed underlying issues. I held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns.
- Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few teammates that was affecting work. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. I said I would look into resolving conflicts and try to redistribute tasks, and that their well-being mattered.
- I felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. I told the team I would create a more supportive, open environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and that we would work together to make the project a success, with their input and well-being crucial.

I do not have access to other characters’ private thoughts, narrator-only facts, or events I did not observe or hear.
